takeaway: Magnesium is absorbed mainly in the duodenum and regulated by the kidneys. Its major renal transport site is the thick ascending limb of Henle, so loop diuretics increase magnesium loss.

question.text: Which one of the following statements regarding magnesium homeostasis is correct?

answer.text: The major site for magnesium transport is in the thick ascending loop of Henle.

lines.text: Dietary magnesium is absorbed mainly in the duodenum, not the large bowel.
The kidneys then regulate the body's magnesium concentration.
Unlike most salts, magnesium is transported in the thick ascending loop of Henle.
So loop diuretics increase magnesium loss, they do not decrease it.
Raised magnesium and calcium levels reduce the amount reabsorbed by the loop of Henle.
So the correct statement is the thick ascending loop of Henle.
